items.excerpt: 11 November 2026• Update: 11 November 2026 WASHINGTON Here’s a rundown of all the news you need to start your Wednesday, including US House blocking effort to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, COP31 leaders’ summit set to open in Türkiye with electrification in focus, and US Secretary of State Marco Rubio calling US-Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi "very productive." The US House of Representatives on Tuesday voted 211-204 to send a resolution to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to committee, effectively killing the effort. Republicans backed the motion 210-1 and were joined by the chamber’s lone independent, while all 203 Democrats who voted opposed it. Republican Congressman Thomas Massie, who authored the resolution, was the only Republican to vote against it. Massie’s resolution, introduced Monday, contained eight articles of impeachment. They accuse Hegseth of waging war with Iran without congressional authorization, carrying out extrajudicial killings in airstrikes against alleged drug-trafficking vessels in the Caribbean Sea, illegally seizing then-Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro, targeting Democratic Senator Mark Kelly and carrying out an unlawful war in Yemen. Hegseth dismissed the effort at a Pentagon news conference earlier Tuesday. - COP31 leaders’ summit set to open in Türkiye with electrification in focus World leaders are set to gather in Türkiye’s Mediterranean city of Antalya on Wednesday for a two-day summit at the COP31 UN climate conference, with the Turkish presidency putting electrification at the center of its push to turn climate pledges into action. Türkiye is seeking support for a proposal to raise electricity’s share of global energy use to 35% by 2035. Turkish Erdogan and UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres are scheduled to address the opening session at the Antalya Expo Center at 12.15 p.m. local time (0915GMT). National statements are due to begin at 2.30 p.m. and continue Thursday. Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, whose country hosted last year’s climate talks, is among those expected to speak Wednesday, along with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, Chinese Vice President Han Zheng and Marshall Islands President Hilda Heine. British Prime Minister Andy Burnham and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian are also expected to address the summit. - US Secretary of State Rubio describes Abu Dhabi talks between US, Russia, Ukraine as 'very productive' US Secretary of State Marco Rubio characterized trilateral negotiations between the US, Russia and Ukraine in Abu Dhabi as "very productive," saying their diplomatic efforts are looking to construct durable security arrangements. "There's a lot of work to be done in that regard. It's not like something that's on the verge of being solved in the next 24 hours or anything like that," Rubio told reporters at a G7 ministerial meeting in France. Rubio said Russian representatives agreeing to the trilateral format and showing up is "good."

US Army Officer Arrested Over Suspected Russian Espionage (UK) Russia and Ukraine held their first US-mediated peace talks in nine months in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday, with both sides agreeing to continue discussions on Wednesday. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio described the meeting as productive, while Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called it constructive and substantive. The discussions covered humanitarian issues, including prisoner exchanges, alongside security guarantees for Ukraine. Washington is also pursuing a broader European security framework, although Moscow and Kyiv remain divided over the sequencing of negotiations and the conditions for ending the war. Russia wants Ukraine to surrender territory and abandon its NATO ambitions, while Kyiv insists on a ceasefire before wider negotiations and rejects territorial concessions. European governments are seeking a role in the process but Moscow has thus far resisted their direct involvement. Fighting continues despite the diplomatic initiative, with both sides conducting long-range strikes against infrastructure. ###### Sources: PBS, Reuters Russia’s one remaining independent newspaper Novaya Gazeta closed its Moscow newsroom on Monday after authorities designated it a foreign agent, its landlord refused to renew its lease and banks stopped processing reader donations. The investigative publication, founded in 1993 with support from former Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev, had faced escalating restrictions, particularly since Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in 2022. ... The newspaper had already lost its media licence, printing facilities and access to its website. Six of its journalists were murdered during its history, including Anna Politkovskaya, who investigated abuses by Russian forces in Chechnya. Founding editor Dmitry Muratov, who shared the 2021 Nobel Peace Prize, criticised the suppression of independent voices and called for the release of political prisoners. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov characterised the closure as normal turnover in the media industry. The newspaper’s journalists rejected that explanation, describing years of mounting state pressure. ... Israel’s newly elected parliament convened on Tuesday, with opposition parties introducing legislation to reverse key policies of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. The proposals include an official inquiry into the October 7, 2023 Hamas-led attacks, repeal of his government’s judicial overhaul and term limits for future prime ministers. However, opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has yet to secure the parliamentary majority needed to replace Netanyahu. His bloc holds 48 seats, against 53 for Netanyahu’s allies, leaving both short of the 61 required. Arab parties control another 19 seats and could support Eisenkot, although some of his coalition partners oppose their inclusion. President Isaac Herzog has given Eisenkot six weeks to form a government. Netanyahu, who remains interim prime minister, has called for a national unity government while attacking the prospect of cooperation with Arab parties. The political impasse leaves Israel’s next government uncertain despite the opposition’s legislative offensive. ... Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps has unveiled footage of an underground missile facility containing ballistic and cruise missiles, while announcing that its self-imposed 2,000km missile range limit has been lifted. The location, age and operational status of the facility could not be independently verified. ... Iranian armed forces chief Major General Ali Abdollahi warned that renewed attacks could trigger retaliation beyond the Middle East. IRGC spokesman Brigadier General Hossein Mohebbi said Iran had also moved missile and drone production underground. The announcement follows American and Israeli strikes intended to weaken Tehran’s missile capabilities. ... The United Nations Human Rights Council has postponed its review of the United States’ human rights record until January after the Trump administration refused to participate. The 47-member body agreed to the delay on Tuesday, marking the second consecutive year Washington has declined to undergo the assessment. The Universal Periodic Review examines all 193 UN member states every four to five years. President Donald Trump’s administration withdrew from the council last year, accusing it of anti-American and anti-Israel bias. The State Department reiterated its rejection of the organisation, while European Union representatives defended the principle of universal scrutiny.

items.excerpt: Both figures were a tenth of a point higher than forecast, and at an annual rate would be well above the Fed's 2% target. The new inflation data heightened concerns that strong consumer and business spending, combined with higher gas prices and supply disruptions stemming from tariffs and global turmoil, are creating increasingly stubborn inflation that could extend beyond temporary spikes in prices at the gas pump. The economy expanded at a 3.4% annual rate in the July-September quarter, mostly driven by consumer spending. ... Gas prices rose 1% from September to October, the government said, a stiff increase but still much lower than in previous months. Gas prices have soared more than 37% from a year ago. Still, oil prices have fallen sharply in recent days on hopes that the Iran conflict is fading, and gas costs have declined this month. Yet there are signs higher energy prices are spreading into other parts of the economy, with air fares, public transportation, and delivery services all jumping in price. Electricity prices rose 0.9% from September to October, the most since April, and grocery prices jumped 0.4%, a painful rise after years of increases. Beef prices rose 0.9% last month, after jumping nearly 14% in the first half of this year. Restaurant prices rose 0.5% from September to October, the most since January 2024. Rising shipping prices, driven up by more expensive gas, have lifted costs for restaurants and grocery stores, which may be passing them on to consumers.

items.excerpt: Nov 10 (Reuters) - Federal Reserve Vice Chair of Supervision Michelle Bowman on Tuesday added her voice to the chorus of colleagues pointing to inflation as their biggest priority, though she stopped short of calling for interest-rate hikes and said she expects price pressures to abate next year as the effect of recent shocks wears off. "Today, I am seeing signs that inflation pressures are persisting, while labor market conditions appear to be firming," Bowman said in remarks prepared for delivery to the Council on Foreign Relations in Washington, DC. "This indicates that there is still work to do to bring inflation closer to 2%." The core personal consumption expenditures price index likely rose 3.3% in October, she said, driven by higher energy prices and AI-related demand. But lack of progress on inflation, she added, has not been driven by the labor market, which has improved but is not overheated. As pressures from the AI buildout and the Middle East conflict "wane or unwind and with no inflationary pressures emerging in the labor market, my forecast is for core PCE inflation to move closer to 2% next year," she said. She cautioned that falling stock prices, rising bond yields and a stronger dollar have tightened financial conditions, creating possible risks to the economy, which has strengthened this year. items.title: Fed officials open door to a quicker round of rate hikes as inflation worsens | live
items.excerpt: WASHINGTON, Nov 10 (Reuters) - The odds that the Federal Reserve may raise interest rates by half a percentage point next month jumped on Tuesday after US data showed prices rising faster than expected in October and policymakers opened the door to a quicker pace of rate hikes. The Consumer Price Index rose 0.4% on a monthly basis in October, down from the 0.6% registered in September as energy inflation receded. The core index excluding volatile food and energy prices, however, rose 0.3% for the third month in a row, evidence of persistent underlying inflation and price pressures spreading through the economy. A few hours before the data was released, Fed Governor Christopher Waller said he planned to support a quarter-point increase at the Fed's December 8-9 meeting unless core CPI came in at 0.3% or more. "In that case, I believe a 50-basis-point hike in the policy rate should be considered at the December meeting," he said at a conference in London hosted by King's Business School and the Money Macro and Finance Society. Sticking with a smaller rate increase, Waller said, risked hurting the Fed's inflation-fighting credibility, given inflation was too high and appeared to be broadening. Economists polled by Reuters had expected core monthly inflation to drop to 0.2% in October. The CPI data and Waller's comments drove a powerful selloff in the US Treasury market, with the yield on 2-year notes — a proxy for Fed policy expectations — rising by the most since early April 2025. By mid-morning, market pricing reflected about a 15% chance of a half-point rate hike before retreating to about 10% in the late afternoon. Over the course of the day, traders also piled into bets the Fed would keep to its usual quarter-point rate hikes but deliver three of them by mid-2027, rather than two as seen before the data.

items.title: The Democratic leadership revolt has a glaring problem
items.excerpt: The Republican leadership fights are over. For Democrats, the pain has only just begun. Why it matters: All the talk about changing party leadership is empty if no one steps up to run. - Senate Republicans demanded more time and deeper conversations about their leadership, but no one stepped forward to challenge John Thune, who won by acclamation. - Democrats are demanding their own conversations about the party's future and the leadership of Chuck Schumer and Hakeem Jeffries. Neither has a challenger. ‼️ The intrigue: Where there was a contested leadership fight, the challenger won. - Rep. Jim Jordan, the Freedom Caucus founding member who spent years tormenting Republican leaders, will now lead the battered House GOP after defeating 12-year leadership veteran Rep. Steve Scalise by 33 votes. - Jordan is the kind of fighter House Republicans want to take on Democrats as they enter the minority, lawmakers told Axios. - "We're gearing up for war. And you're talking to a guy who's known as a hammer. You know we need someone who can punch hard, and I think that he'll do that," Rep. Randy Fine (R-Fla.) told Axios. 🤺 Zoom in: No such fighter has emerged to challenge Democratic leaders from within their ranks, and Schumer said he is "confident I will be elected majority leader." - The closest thing to a challenge is Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.), who's listening to calls to run for Democratic leader while also considering a presidential campaign. It's hard to do both. - Meanwhile, opposition to Schumer is building: " [T]he time is now for change," Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.) said Tuesday. He appeared with Sen. Elissa Slotkin (D-Mich.), who said she's not "actively seeking the job" but demanded a plan for change. 🏛️ Over in the House, Jeffries is dismissive of the idea that anyone would challenge him after the midterms gave him a massive majority. - "You think I don't have the vote nailed down? I guess we'll find out next Wednesday," he told reporters on Monday. - Some of his new members are signaling that they're not afraid to defy their new leaders. Rep.-elect Don Leonard (D-Ohio) said it "aches" his heart to potentially oppose the first Black speaker, "but Rome is burning." - But other new members are on Jeffries' side, like Reps.-elect Marni von Wilpert (D-Calif.), Denise Powell (D-Neb.) and Cait Conley (D-N.Y.). 🤝 Jeffries also has high-profile progressive incumbents on board, such as Rep. Greg Casar (D-Texas), Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-N.Y.), Pramila Jayapal (D-Wash.) and Ro Khanna (D-Calif.). - "There is one candidate in this race, Hakeem Jeffries, and I think that everyone is far more concerned about what that leadership means, what is it promising?" Ocasio-Cortez told reporters on Tuesday. Between the lines: Thune and Jordan don't have much of a relationship; Thune had left the House for the Senate two years before Jordan arrived.

items.excerpt: Not only does the party in power historically suffer defeats in midterm elections, but Donald Trump’s approval ratings had cratered with voters, even on issues that he had previously polled well on, while Democrats had surged in special and off-year elections. ... Congress still has a long to-do list to push through before the year ends and the new political configuration is cemented. Government funding runs out on 11 December and must be extended, ideally through next September. A big defense policy bill remains unfinished, as does a long-delayed agricultural measure. All of this legislation will need buy-in from both parties to advance.

items.title: Entertainment news roundup: 11 November 2026 | SVCZZ
items.excerpt: Ramayana: Rise of a Legend has become the first Indian film to top the UK and Ireland weekend box office, taking £1.7 million from 364 cinemas over 6 to 8 November 2026 and finishing second globally for the weekend behind Godzilla Minus Zero. HBO’s Harry Potter put its three young leads on character posters, with the first season premiering on 25 December 2026. The roundup also remembers two actors: Toukie Smith, Eva Rawley on 227, and veteran Nollywood actor Diewait Ikpechukwu. ## Box office The £1.7 million weekend for Ramayana: Rise of a Legend across 364 UK and Ireland cinemas, 6 to 8 November 2026, made it the first Indian film to top the weekend chart there, on Comscore figures reported by Hollywood Reporter India. Globally it finished second for the weekend, behind Godzilla Minus Zero. Kabaddi 5: After the Final Match has passed Rs 12 crore at the domestic box office, with Film Development Board figures released on 9 November 2026 putting its gross at Rs 12,39,92,245 from 405,884 tickets as of 8 November 2026. Lalibazar still leads the domestic collections in the Film Development Board’s latest figures, published on 9 November 2026: Rs 93.2 million after 51 days in cinemas, ahead of Roll No. 1 at Rs 17.4 million and I Am Jit Bahadur at Rs 3.1 million. The figures cover Lalibazar, now into its second month on release. ## Remembering Toukie Smith has died aged 74. The model and actress, who played Eva Rawley on 227 and appeared on Miami Vice, died on 4 November 2026 in a New York hospital after a long battle with multiple sclerosis, her twins Airyn and Julian confirming her death to The Hollywood Reporter. Diewait Ikpechukwu, the veteran Nollywood actor and former footballer known for playing traditional rulers, has died aged 71 after a prolonged illness. He died on 5 November 2026, and the death was announced the following day by Abubakar Yakubu, National President of the Actors Guild of Nigeria. ## Trailers and first looks HBO’s three character posters for Harry Potter give each of the young leads the same treatment: Dominic McLaughlin as Harry, Arabella Stanton as Hermione and Alastair Stout as Ron, wands held upright down the centre of the frame under the line “The first year begins”. The motion versions carry a first snippet of Hans Zimmer’s score, and the eight-episode first season, Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone, premieres on 25 December 2026 on HBO and HBO Max. Disney and National Geographic have announced The Real Frozen, a natural history series in which Idina Menzel, Kristen Bell and Jonathan Groff return to narrate, with Josh Gad making special appearances as Olaf. It will air on National Geographic and Disney+, and no premiere date has been announced. Salman Khan shared the official trailer for Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace online on 10 November 2026. The war drama, inspired by the June 2020 Galwan Valley clash and directed by Apoorva Lakhia, opens in cinemas on 4 December 2026. The theatrical trailer for Gunmaaster G9 is due out today, 11 November 2026, ahead of the Emraan Hashmi romantic action film’s cinema release on 27 November 2026. Danny Boyle’s Ink, a drama about the birth of The Sun newspaper, has a new trailer, with Guy Pearce as Rupert Murdoch and Jack O’Connell as Larry Lamb. It opens in UK and Ireland cinemas on 8 January 2027. Jesse Eisenberg’s The Debut also has a new trailer, starring Julianne Moore and Paul Giamatti alongside Halle Bailey, ahead of its theatrical release on 11 December 2026. Dario Russo’s comedy The Fox follows the same pattern, its new trailer putting Jai Courtney and Emily Browning front and centre, with Olivia Colman and Sam Neill in one of his final performances, for a 4 December 2026 cinema release. Mouli’s dark comedy DNK, about robbery and crime, has its trailer out ahead of a 13 November 2026 cinema release. Ravi Teja launched the trailer. ## Reviews and reactions First reviews for Steps, Netflix’s animated Cinderella reimagining starring Ali Wong as Lilith, landed on 9 November 2026 and run mostly favourable: three of the four reviews quoted are positive, with The Hollywood Reporter dissenting. It streams on Netflix from 20 November 2026. Press screenings in New York and London left first reactions to Ebenezer mostly positive. Johnny Depp plays Scrooge in Ti West’s gothic reimagining of A Christmas Carol, which opens in cinemas on 13 November 2026. ... Netflix has renewed The Later Daters for season 2 with a celebrity cast that includes Vivica A. Fox, Christie Brinkley, Margaret Cho, Caroline Rhea and Pebe Sebert. It premieres on 30 December 2026. ... 9 to 5 leaves Netflix on 1 December 2026, with 30 November 2026 the last day to watch it, and no new streaming home confirmed.
